title: The order approved (1216)
hookLine: approved at last, Dominic's few friars scatter to the university towns

lines: A NAME, AND THE POPE'S APPROVAL.
cards: A small group of men in Toulouse. They have a name now, the pope's approval, and a future together. The sensible move is to stay: build the house, grow slowly, side by side, under the eye of the man who gathered them.
Instead, the early accounts say, Dominic tells them to split up. Some to Paris. Some to Bologna.
Some back to Spain. The brothers object: too few, too new, they hardly know the work yet. He sends them anyway.
Today, the order approved, and the first thing it did with its approval: scatter.

teach.h: THE ORDER OF PREACHERS: NAMED FOR A TASK.
teach.b: On paper the approval is quiet: the bishop of Rome signs, and a band of preachers from the south of France becomes an order of the whole Church. Their name says the job: the Order of Preachers.
Named not for a place or a house, but for a task, and a task like that pulls you outward. Near its end, Mark's Gospel has Jesus sending his followers out.
In the Douay-Rheims: "Go ye into the whole world, and preach the gospel to every creature." Dominic seems to have taken that at its word.

teach.h: GRAIN HEAPED ROTS; GRAIN SCATTERED GROWS.
teach.b: A saying credited to him, in substance: grain heaped up in a barn goes bad; grain scattered on a field bears fruit. So the brothers went where the people were, to the cities: markets, workshops, crowds of strangers.

teach.h: TO THE CITIES AND THE UNIVERSITIES.
teach.b: And in some cities, something newer still, the universities, full of young men arguing about everything. The friars went straight in.

teach.h: HE HAD FEW BROTHERS, AND GAVE THEM AWAY.
teach.b: They studied there, preached there, and found new brothers there, as students and teachers asked for the habit.

teach.h: GO YE INTO THE WHOLE WORLD.
teach.b: That choice shaped the whole order. The Rule of Saint Benedict asks a monk to promise stability, to stay with one community. A friar's life was built for the road.
And the approval didn't make Dominic careful. He had very few brothers, and he gave them away.

how: Dominican friars live in communities, often in cities and near universities, and preach, teach and serve as chaplains; they write O.P., for the Order of Preachers, after their names.

games.q: you lead a tiny new community, just approved by the pope. your brothers want to stay together and grow slowly. what do you do?
o: send them out to the cities and universities.
wait for more recruits before you decide.
games.why: the early accounts say Dominic scattered them almost at once, over their objections. grain heaped up rots; scattered, it grows.

practice: Bring to mind one student you know, a kid at the kitchen table, a niece away at college, a coworker in night classes, maybe you, and see them at the desk, the screen bright, the coffee gone cold.
Then add someone you'll never meet, alone in a library right now, stuck on the same page; if you pray, say a Hail Mary for both, and if not, wish them a clear head and a good teacher.

wordCard.voice: The order approved. A small band became an order of the whole Church, and then scattered. This week ran from Francis on the bare ground to Dominic's friars on the road. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the Order of Preachers, the Dominicans' official name. it's why friars write O.P. after their names.

carryVoice: Your line: to the cities. Grain kept in the barn goes bad; scattered, it grows. Until tomorrow.
